title: phy_boundary
description: GENERATED artifact (unlike register_map.schema.json, which is an input contract): dv_harness/phy_boundary.py derives this from a real RTL port table -- the same verible-parsed dut_facts.rtl.files[].modules[] that env_manifest.py already produces -- plus a project-declared PHY/controller module pair. It answers exactly one question the asset-processing table assigns to it: at which layer may a bind be mounted, given where the serial/parallel boundary between PHY and controller actually falls. Nothing here is naming-derived: every classification carries the real port widths it was computed from, mirroring connectivity.py's determine_role_from_port_direction() discipline of taking structural evidence only. The declared module pair is a real project fact the project supplies (which module IS the PHY); this file never guesses it from a name.

status.description: EXTRACTED when a real RTL port table for both declared modules was parsed. NOT_AVAILABLE (with a real `reason`) when no RTL was supplied or a declared module is absent from it -- never a fabricated boundary.

boundary_signals.description: Ports present on BOTH declared modules' port lists -- real structural evidence of a shared boundary signal set, not a name-similarity match.

width.description: Real bit width parsed from the port's own declared data_type packed range; null when the declaration carries no resolvable literal range (e.g. a parameterized width) -- null is reported honestly, never defaulted to 1.

width_source.description: The literal data_type text the width was parsed from, so a reviewer can re-derive it.

direction_opposed.description: True when the two modules declare opposite directions for this signal (input vs output) -- the expected shape of a real point-to-point boundary connection.

kind.description: SERIAL: the boundary's data-bearing signals are all narrow (<= SERIAL_MAX_WIDTH bits), i.e. a line-rate lane pair no VIP monitor can decode without a PHY model. PARALLEL: at least one data-bearing signal is a bus of >= PARALLEL_MIN_WIDTH bits, i.e. a PIPE/UTMI-style symbol boundary where transactions are observable. MIXED: both are genuinely present (a PHY exposing both its serial pins and its parallel controller-facing port). UNDECIDABLE: no resolvable widths -- routed to the question queue, never guessed.

tier.description: B1_DECLARED: the project explicitly declared the boundary kind and this file records it. B2_STRUCTURAL_WIDTH: derived from real parsed port widths. B3_UNDECIDABLE: neither available.

mount_layer.description: controller_phy_parallel_boundary: mount the bind at the parallel controller<->PHY port set named in parallel_signals -- protocol transactions are observable there. serial_boundary_not_bindable: the only boundary is serial; a protocol VIP monitor bound there sees line-rate symbols it cannot decode without a PHY model, so this is reported as NOT bindable rather than emitting a bind that would silently monitor nothing. requires_human_decision: UNDECIDABLE classification -- goes to the question queue.

recommended_bind_signals.description: The concrete boundary signal names a bind at mount_layer would connect through its own port list -- per CLAUDE.md Bind-Location Rule 3, clock/reset and these signals go through the bind instance's port list, never a cross-level hierarchical reference.
